messages:
maya_support: Hey team — customer (acme) reports their prod pods suddenly get NXDOMAIN for our service endpoint hostnames after last night's cert rotation. They see app-level 502s + downstream NXDOMAIN in logs. Can we triage?

acme_agent: Yep. Started ~2025-01-31 02:10 UTC. Apps log: "lookup api.payments.svc.acme-corp.internal: no such host". We ran a quick curl -> failed with "could not resolve host". No infra changes on their side other than a credential rotation.

maya_support: Can you paste a couple diagnostic outputs? dig +short from one of the failing pods and from host network would be great. Also pod's /etc/resolv.conf and node-local-dns logs if possible.

acme_agent: Here you go (sanitized):
```
# from pod 
$ cat /etc/resolv.conf
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 127.0.0.53
options ndots:5

$ dig +short api.payments.svc.acme-corp.internal
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +short api.payments.svc.acme-corp.internal
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1

# from node (uses AmazonProvidedDNS) 
$ dig +short @10.0.0.2 api.payments.svc.acme-corp.internal
52.44.11.22
```

acme_agent: node sees the correct IP, pod sees NXDOMAIN.

owen_sre: Interesting — node resolves fine but pod via node-local (127.0.0.53) is returning NXDOMAIN. Two likely causes: (1) node-local-dns negative cache holding an NXDOMAIN from a forwarder/stub that answered earlier, or (2) resolver rule / stub domain pointing to on-prem DNS that returns NXDOMAIN for that exact fqdn (split-horizon).

owen_sre: Can you grab node-local-dns logs for the timeframe and search for queries to api.payments.svc.acme-corp.internal and upstream responses? Also share iptables/egress allowlist for the node that might be blocking access to the AWS resolver IPs that node-local falls back to.

acme_agent: Logs attached (excerpt):
```
2025-01-31T02:09:34Z query: api.payments.svc.acme-corp.internal -> upstream 172.31.100.5 (forwarder)
2025-01-31T02:09:34Z upstream response: NXDOMAIN
2025-01-31T02:09:34Z cached negative entry TTL 300s
```

lia_net: Aha — 172.31.100.5 is their on-prem DNS forwarder over the VPC resolver outbound endpoint. Looks like a stub/resolver rule we installed to reach on-prem is catching the entire "svc.acme-corp.internal" suffix and returning NXDOMAIN for the endpoint hostnames (split-horizon). Node-local cached the NXDOMAIN and returns it to pods.

lia_net: This is distinctive from a classic private hosted zone shadowing case. Here the forwarder answers explicitly NXDOMAIN. Node-local respects the negative cache and serves NXDOMAIN until TTL expires.

owen_sre: Short-term mitigations: 
- Delete the negative cache entry by restarting node-local-dns on the node(s) (quick but disruptive) OR use kubectl exec into the node-local pod and send SIGHUP if supported.
- Temporarily add a resolver rule with higher priority that forwards the exact hostname (api.payments.svc.acme-corp.internal) to AmazonProvidedDNS/AWS resolver instead of the on-prem forwarder.

acme_agent: Restarting node-local on one node cleared it for that node; pods started resolving again. But they have many nodes so not ideal.

maya_support: Long-term fixes: 
- Narrow the on-prem resolver rule so it only handles the internal zones that truly need on-prem answers (e.g., corp.internal) and not the service endpoint suffixes; or add explicit exceptions for "svc.<tenant>.internal".
- If the service endpoint is backed by AWS PrivateLink/Interface Endpoint, ensure there's no stub domain that forwards those suffixes to on-prem. The correct behavior is to let AmazonProvidedDNS resolve to the interface ENI IPs.
- Optionally, instruct on-prem DNS team to return a referral or NXDOMAIN only when appropriate. Returning NXDOMAIN for names owned by other systems will break split-horizon setups.

lia_net: Also verify VPC resolver inbound/outbound endpoints and their rule priority. We had a case where a catch-all rule was created with lower numeric priority but since it matched first it got applied — double-check rule's order.

nowen_sre: TLS note: the cert rotation earlier probably unrelated to DNS NXDOMAIN, but once DNS is fixed customers reported a TLS mismatch for a subset of requests that use a custom CNAME -> service endpoint. If you still see TLS failures after DNS fix, collect SNI and the cert presented (openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername <host>) and paste here.

acme_agent: Verified: after restarting node-local on test nodes, DNS and requests succeed and TLS looks fine. We'll roll the resolver rule change to prod: remove the broad forwarder for "svc.acme-corp.internal" and only keep the corp.* zones.

maya_support: Great. Can you also add a note to the customer's onboarding doc warning about creating wide stub rules that forward tenant svc namespaces to on-prem? I'll follow up with a KB item we can link. :white_check_mark:

deploybot: automated note: handled-by-support #1738501234 status=resolved tags=[dns,split-horizon,node-local]
